article_title: Impact of automated scoring on interpreting performance and self-regulated learning: evidence from a pedagogical experiment
citation: Chen C and Liu T (2026) Impact of automated scoring on interpreting performance and self-regulated learning: evidence from a pedagogical experiment. Front. Psychol. 17:1867463. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1867463
title: Zimmerman's three-phase cyclical SRL model as a lens for locating which phases automated feedback reaches
description: The study adopts Zimmerman's (2000, 2002) three-phase model of self-regulated learning — forethought, performance, and self-reflection — as its primary analytical lens, treating each of the system's four feedback dimensions as an input into self-judgment. The model is chosen because it "can accommodate the possibility... that a feedback intervention reaches some phases but not others, instead of treating SRL as a single global capacity". The article's contribution is specifying which phase automated scoring reaches: it reinforced the performance phase, reached self-reflection only in its lower-effort form, and left forethought largely untouched.
requirements: Evaluation of automated feedback tools should be phase-differentiated rather than global, measuring SRL phases individually instead of relying on a single overall score
constraints: Motivational constructs such as self-efficacy are treated as forethought subprocesses rather than a separate phase, following Zimmerman's placement of self-motivation beliefs within forethought
target_learners: student interpreters using automated scoring systems
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning across forethought, performance, and self-reflection phases
examples: The questionnaire's four measurement blocks (Pre-learning Planning, Execution and Monitoring, Evaluation and Reflection, Emotional Motivation) were mapped onto the model's phases
key_sources: Chen C and Liu T (2026) Impact of automated scoring on interpreting performance and self-regulated learning: evidence from a pedagogical experiment. Front. Psychol. 17:1867463. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1867463

article_title: A Review of Self-regulated Learning: Six Models and Four Directions for Research
citation: Panadero E. (2017). A Review of Self-regulated Learning: Six Models and Four Directions for Research. Front. Psychol. 8:422. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00422
title: Zimmerman's Cyclical Phases model of SRL: forethought, performance, self-reflection
description: Zimmerman's Cyclical Phases model organizes self-regulated learning into three recursive phases. Per the review, in the forethought phase "the students analyze the task, set goals, plan how to reach them" energized by motivational beliefs; in the performance phase they execute the task while monitoring progress and using self-control strategies; in the self-reflection phase they assess performance and make attributions whose self-reactions influence later task engagement. The review treats it as the individual-level process model comparable to the other five SRL models analyzed.
requirements: Describes SRL at the individual level, parallel to the other reviewed models
target_learning_goals: strategic self-regulated learning
examples: Cleary et al. trained 50 college students in basketball free throws across conditions training different numbers of SRL phases
key_sources: Panadero E. (2017). A Review of Self-regulated Learning: Six Models and Four Directions for Research. Front. Psychol. 8:422. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00422

article_title: A Review of Self-regulated Learning: Six Models and Four Directions for Research
citation: Panadero, E. (2017). A Review of Self-regulated Learning: Six Models and Four Directions for Research. Frontiers in Psychology, 8:422. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00422
title: Zimmerman's Cyclical Phases model of SRL: forethought, performance, and self-reflection
description: Zimmerman's Cyclical Phases model organizes self-regulated learning into three recurring phases. As the review states, "Zimmerman's (2000) SRL model is organized in three phases: forethought, performance and self-reflection". In forethought students analyze the task, set goals and plan; in performance they execute the task while monitoring progress and using self-control strategies; in self-reflection they assess performance and make attributions whose self-reactions influence later task approaches. The review analyzes this model as Zimmerman's contribution comparable in level to the other five SRL models.
requirements: Students must engage in task analysis, goal setting and planning before performance for the cycle to operate as described
constraints: The review analyzes the Cyclical Phases model rather than Zimmerman's Triadic or Multi-Level models, to keep comparison at the same level as the other models
target_learners: school and college students learning academic and athletic skills
target_learning_goals: strategic, self-regulated approach to learning tasks
examples: The review reports Cleary et al. (2006) trained 50 college students in basketball free throws across conditions training one, two, or three SRL phases
key_sources: Panadero, E. (2017). A Review of Self-regulated Learning: Six Models and Four Directions for Research. Frontiers in Psychology, 8:422. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00422

article_title: Fostering regulatory processes using computational scaffolding
citation: Leonardo Silva, António Mendes, Anabela Gomes, Gabriel Fortes. (2023). Fostering regulation of learning processes among programming students using computational scaffolding. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn (2023) 18:67–100. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-023-09388-y
title: Zimmerman's three-phase cyclical SRL model as the design reference for regulatory scaffolding
description: The article uses Zimmerman's model, which "describes SRL as a cyclical process comprising three phases": forethought (understanding and planning the task with motivational beliefs), performance (metacognitive monitoring, cognitive strategies, motivational evaluation during execution), and self-reflection (judgments about performance and reflection on improvement). Knowledge acquired feeds the next cycle. The model "was used as a reference in the design of our proposed regulatory scaffolding", with scaffolds categorized by phase (Fig. 1).
requirements: Scaffolds must be aligned to the three cyclical phases (forethought, performance, self-reflection) so students are supported at planning, execution, and reflection stages
constraints: The authors note the model conceptualizes the student as an individual in isolation from the social environment, which has been subject of critique
target_learners: novice programming students in online introductory programming courses
target_learning_goals: planning, monitoring, and self-reflection during programming learning
examples: RESPE scaffolds such as the learning journal and software planner were categorized by Zimmerman's SRL phases (Fig. 1).
key_sources: Leonardo Silva, António Mendes, Anabela Gomes, Gabriel Fortes. (2023). Fostering regulation of learning processes among programming students using computational scaffolding. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn (2023) 18:67–100. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-023-09388-y

article_title: Effects of short- and long-term prompting in learning journals on strategy use, self-efficacy, and learning outcomes
citation: Nadja M. Gentner, Lisa Respondek, Tina Seufert. (2024). Effects of short- and long-term prompting in learning journals on strategy use, self-efficacy, and learning outcomes. Instructional Science (2024) 52:919–950. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-024-09671-x
title: Zimmerman's cyclical three-phase model of self-regulated learning (forethinking, performance, self-reflection)
description: The article adopts Zimmerman's (2005) model as its theoretical framework: self-regulation "refers to self-generated thoughts, feelings, and actions that are planned and cyclically adapted to the attainment of personal goals". It integrates cognitive, metacognitive, emotion-affective, and motivational components in three phases — forethought (task analysis, planning, strategy selection), performance (applying strategies, monitoring), and self-reflection (judging the process, selecting regulation strategies). Because the model treats self-regulated learning as a process unfolding over time, the authors chose it as the basis for their longitudinal design with continuous weekly measurement.
requirements: Continuous measurements over time are needed to capture the development of self-regulation components across phases.
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning strategy use and motivation in coursework
examples: The study measured cognitive and metacognitive strategy use and self-efficacy weekly at t1–t8 across two course units, following the model's process view.

article_title: Self-regulated learning and video annotation in a high school acting classroom
citation: Hengtao Tang, Jessica Perry Ellison. (2025). Self-regulated learning and video annotation in a high school acting classroom. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-024-09699-z
title: Zimmerman's cyclical self-regulated learning model (forethought, performance/volition, self-reflection)
description: The study's theoretical framework is Zimmerman's (2000) model, which "illustrates self-regulated learning as a recursive cycle" in which learners prepare in the forethought phase (task analysis and self-motivation beliefs), perform and monitor in the performance/volition phase (self-control and self-observation), and reflect in the self-reflection phase (self-evaluation and causal attribution). The intervention mapped weekly goal-setting forms, rehearsal with VideoAnt annotation, and progress reports onto these three phases.
requirements: Interventions must integrate elements from each of the three SRL phases, as the six-week intervention did
constraints: The article states the full scope of SRL strategies was not addressed due to the limited time span of the study
target_learners: secondary school students aged 14-18 in performing arts classes
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning skills
acting skills including physicality, vocal performance, and character analysis
examples: Weekly goal-setting forms supported forethought; filmed rehearsals annotated in VideoAnt supported self-observation; weekly progress reports supported self-evaluation

citation: Patrick Sins, Renske de Leeuw, Jaap de Brouwer, Emmy Vrieling-Teunter. (2024). Promoting explicit instruction of strategies for self-regulated learning: evaluating a teacher professional development program in primary education. Metacognition and Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11409-023-09368-5
title: Zimmerman's cyclic model of self-regulated learning: forethought, performance and self-reflection phases
description: The article presents Zimmerman's cyclic model as one of the predominant process models of SRL, grounded in social cognitive theory. It "describes SRL in terms of three cyclical phases: a forethought phase, a performance phase and a self-reflection phase", covering orienting and goal setting, strategy deployment with monitoring, and evaluation of the learning process. The article uses this model, alongside component models, as the conceptual basis for the SRL strategies addressed in iSELF and its observation instrument.
requirements: SRL is conceptualized as an interplay between cognitive, metacognitive, motivational and behavioral processes oriented toward goal attainment
constraints: the phases do not follow a strictly linear sequence and can take place simultaneously depending on the learner, feedback and plan changes
target_learning_goals: planning, monitoring and evaluating the learning process

citation: Kitsantas, A., Bembenutty, H., Cleary, T. J., Alexander, P. A., DiBenedetto, M. K., Kaplan, A., Kolovelonis, A., Mandell, B. E., Martin, A. J., McCrudden, M. title: Zimmerman's cyclical phase model of self-regulated learning: forethought, performance, and self-reflection operating recursively
description: The article describes Zimmerman's cyclical phase model of SRL as his most enduring theoretical contribution. It articulates three interrelated phases that "operate recursively as learners plan, execute, and evaluate their actions": forethought, performance, and self-reflection. The model gave researchers a structured lens for investigating SRL mechanisms and gave educators a basis for designing interventions that foster strategic, motivated, independent learners, framing SRL as central to academic success and lifelong learning.
requirements: SRL must be treated as a dynamic, iterative process with distinct phases rather than a single stable construct
constraints: The model integrates motivational, emotional, and cognitive processes across three interacting phases as the article describes it; the tribute does not report new empirical tests of the model
target_learners: learners across academic, sport, music, and health domains
target_learning_goals: strategic, motivated, and independent self-regulated learning
examples: Colleagues report using the cyclical model as a core framework in empirical studies, formative assessment and feedback research, teacher education games, and doctoral seminars

title: Zimmerman's four-level developmental model of self-regulation: observation, emulation, self-control, self-regulation
description: The article presents Zimmerman's four-level developmental model as a landmark framework for fostering strategic learning across developmental stages. It "outlines a progression from observation to emulation, followed by self-control and ultimately self-regulation," showing how learners internalize effective strategies through social modeling, scaffolded practice, and increasing independence. By mapping a path from external guidance to internal control, it gives educators a roadmap for cultivating SRL competencies.
requirements: Social modeling and scaffolded practice opportunities are needed as learners move from external guidance toward internal control
constraints: The tribute reports the model's application to motor and sport skills instruction and notes a future direction of personalizing it for students with varying competencies; it reports no new test of the model itself
target_learners: students learning motor and sport skills
target_learning_goals: gradual internalization of effective learning strategies and self-regulatory competence

description: The article reports that Zimmerman (1998) reframed academic studying as a dynamic, self-regulated process involving six interrelated dimensions: "motivation, method, time, physical environment, performance, and self-reflection." article_title: The Binet-Simon Scale and the Yerkes point Scale - A comparative study based on the examination of 100 cases.
citation: Zimmerman, J. (1914). The Binet-Simon Scale and the Yerkes Point Scale: A Comparative Study Based on the Examination of 100 Cases. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://psycnet.apa.org/journal/edu
title: Zimmerman's 100-case comparative dataset of Binet-Simon and Yerkes Point Scale examinations
description: Chart I presents case-level results for 100 children aged six to sixteen, each examined personally by the author with both scales at one sitting. For each case it records sex, language grouping (English vs non-English-speaking parents), chronological age, Point Scale score and age norm, the coefficient of intellectual ability, mental ages from both scales, and status ratings with their difference. Cases are numbered to avoid disclosing names, and a star marks children in ungraded classes.
requirements: Examinations were conducted under favorable conditions, with no third person present, after rapport was established with the child.
constraints: The sample is a referred clinical population from public schools, the Bureau of Attendance, and parents, so most cases rate below chronological age.
target_learners: school-age children six to sixteen examined in an educational clinic
target_learning_goals: measurement of children's mental age and intellectual ability for placement decisions
examples: The Binet-Simon scale used was the 1911 revision translated by Dr. Clara H. Town; the Point Scale was that given by Professor Yerkes in A Point Scale for Measuring Mental Ability.
key_sources: Zimmerman, J. (1914). The Binet-Simon Scale and the Yerkes Point Scale: A Comparative Study Based on the Examination of 100 Cases. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://psycnet.apa.org/journal/edu

article_title: Research Problems Raised in Recent Issues of Educational Periodicals.
citation: Zirbes, L. (1922). Research problems raised in recent issues of educational periodicals. The Journal of Educational Psychology, 13(1), 1-6.
title: Zirbes's seven-category classification of educational research problems raised in periodicals
description: The article organizes the unsolved problems it assembles into seven headings: mental tests, curriculum studies, administration and supervision, educational test problems, learning studies, rating-scale problems, and the need for statistical devices and methods. Each category lists the problems with periodical and page references so researchers can find the original statements. The author reports that classification "was not seriously hampered by overlapping," and that counting references per heading yields relative frequencies of the grouped problems.
requirements: Access to the nine searched 1921 periodicals so that each problem can be located in its original setting via the printed periodical and page references
constraints: The search was confined to the three most recent (autumn 1921) issues of the listed periodicals, except as noted, so the taxonomy reflects a restricted body of literature
target_learners: educational researchers and graduate students in education
target_learning_goals: identifying urgent, unsolved problems for educational research
examples: Category II lists curriculum problems such as scientific determination of curricula in history and reconstruction of college curricula in terms of individual differences
key_sources: Zirbes, L. (1922). Research problems raised in recent issues of educational periodicals. The Journal of Educational Psychology, 13(1), 1-6. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0074413

article_title: Research Problems Raised in Recent Issues of Educational Periodicals.
citation: Zirbes, L. (1922). Research problems raised in recent issues of educational periodicals. The Journal of Educational Psychology, 13(1), 1-6.
title: Zirbes's periodical-search method for rescuing statements of unsolved research problems
description: The article describes a search procedure that reads recent issues of nine educational periodicals and extracts statements of unsolved research problems, which are usually mentioned incidentally in connection with practical situations. Problems are recorded with periodical number and page references "so that those who are in a position to conduct research may readily find the original statement of any problem in its setting," and original phrasing is retained wherever possible. The article is presented as one of a series intended to define research trends and hasten solutions by re-statement and accessibility.
requirements: A defined, restricted set of periodical issues so that frequency of mention is meaningful within single volumes
constraints: The search was limited to autumn 1921 issues because several publications lack summer numbers, and the author argues several carefully limited searches serve better than one more inclusive investigation
target_learning_goals: locating and formulating researchable problems in education
examples: The searched list comprised nine periodicals including the Psychological Bulletin, School and Society (10 issues), and the Teachers College Record

article_title: A randomized controlled trial on the digital socio-emotional competence training Zirkus Empathico for preschoolers
citation: Naumann, S., Bayer, M., Kirst, S., van der Meer, E. & Dziobek, I. (2023). A randomized controlled trial on the digital socio-emotional competence training Zirkus Empathico for preschoolers. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-023-00169-8
title: Zirkus Empathico touchscreen application for socio-emotional competence training
description: Zirkus Empathico is a touchscreen application that "targets awareness and differentiation of own and others ' emotions, empathy, and prosocial behaviors through interactions with naturalistic video sequences of facial expressions and social situations". It comprises four modules: a virtual emotion manikin for specifying own emotional states on arousal and valence dimensions, facial expression labeling, identifying emotions from emotion-eliciting video contexts, and choosing prosocial reactions to others' emotions. Developed from autism-specific behavior therapy principles, it was evaluated here with typically developing preschoolers at home over 6 weeks.
requirements: Delivered on a tablet-PC at home with a weekly engagement of minimum 60 min over 6 weeks, with parents assisting only minimally
constraints: Originally developed for children with autism and developmental level 5–10 years; the study sample was middle to upper-class families
target_learning_goals: Empathy (cognitive and affective)
Emotion recognition
Prosocial behavior
Awareness and differentiation of own and others' emotions
examples: In the RCT, children practiced at home for 6 weeks with a weekly minimum of 60 min, monitored and capped at 30 min daily via the Screen Time tracking application

article_title: Development and validation of a learning analytics rubric for self-regulated learning
citation: de Barba, P. G., Oliveira, E. A., & English, N. (2025). Development and validation of a learning analytics rubric for self-regulated learning. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10521-x
title: Zimmerman's cyclical three-phase model of self-regulated learning
description: The socio-cognitive perspective on self-regulated learning, primarily advanced by Zimmerman (2002), conceptualizes SRL as a cyclical process involving three phases: forethought, performance, and self-reflection. During the forethought phase, students engage in task analysis and activate self-motivational beliefs. The performance phase involves self-control and self-observation. In the self-reflection phase, students evaluate their performance and make attributions about causes of results. This model emphasizes that self-regulated learning is not a fixed trait but rather a context-specific set of processes that students can develop over time.
requirements: Assessment should capture the temporal and contextual dimensions of regulatory processes rather than treating them as static attributes
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning across forethought, performance, and self-reflection phases
examples: The article maps its eight indicators onto Zimmerman's cyclical model, with indicators 5 and 7 reflecting forethought phase activities

article_title: The Effect of Self-Regulated Jigsaw IV on University Students' Academic Achievements and Attitudes towards English Course
citation: Esin Özdemir, Ali Arslan. (2016). The Effect of Self-regulated Jigsaw IV on University Students' Academic Achievements and Attitudes towards English Course. Journal of Education and Training Studies. http://dx.doi.org/10.11114/jets.v4i5.1453
title: Zimmerman's cyclical three-phase model of self-regulated learning
description: The article adopts Zimmerman's cyclical model of self-regulated learning, which "consists of the forethought, performance and self-reflection cyclical phases in the acquisition of self -regulated learning". Forethought covers goal setting, strategic planning, self-efficacy and task interest before performance; performance control covers self-instruction, attention focusing, task strategies and metacognitive monitoring during learning; self-reflection covers self-evaluation, causal attribution and self-satisfaction after performance. The article uses these three phases as the coding framework for analyzing student interview data.
requirements: Students are motivated to adopt the strategies, since motivational and cognitive aspects are intertwined
target_learners: university students learning a foreign language
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning skills such as goal setting, monitoring and self-evaluation
examples: The interview data in section 3.2 were analyzed with the forethought, performance control and self-reflection phases as sub-categories

article_title: The Effect of Self-Regulation Based Strategic Reading Education on Comprehension, Motivation, and Self-Regulation Skills
citation: Tuncay Türkben. (2019). The Effect of Self -Regulation Based Strategic Reading Education on Comprehension, Motivation, and Self-Regulation Skills. International Journal of Progressive Education, Volume 15 Number 4. https://doi.org/10.29329/ijpe.2019.203.3
title: Zimmerman's three-phase sociocognitive self-regulated learning model (forethought, performance, self-reflection)
description: The article frames its intervention with Zimmerman and Pintrich's sociocognitive self-regulation models, in which self-regulation is "not as an intellectual skill or academic trait but as a self-oriented process in which students transform their intellectual skills into academic skills". The model organizes self-regulation into three phases: "forethought phase, performance phase and self -reflection phases". Forethought covers task analysis (goal setting, strategic planning) and self-motivation beliefs; performance covers self-control and self-observation; self-reflection covers self-judgment and self-reaction. The study's lesson plans were structured directly around these phases.
requirements: Students follow an active path in terms of cognition, motivation, and behavior in their learning processes
constraints: The article frames the model within social cognitive theory, in which learning is influenced by personal, environmental, and behavioral factors
target_learning_goals: reading comprehension
reading motivation
self-regulation skills
examples: The study's lesson plans were organized in Forethought, Performance, and Self-Reflection phases in alignment with self-regulating strategies

article_title: Self-Regulated Strategy Instruction for Developing Speaking Proficiency and Reducing Speaking Anxiety of Egyptian University Students
citation: El-Sakka, S. M. F. (2016). Self-Regulated Strategy Instruction for Developing Speaking Proficiency and Reducing Speaking Anxiety of Egyptian University Students. English Language Teaching, 9(12). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v9n12p22
title: Zimmerman's three-phase cyclical model of self-regulated learning as the framework for speaking instruction
description: The article grounds its intervention in the cyclical self-regulated learning model introduced by Pintrich and Zusho (2002) and Zimmerman (2000), whose "three main phases of self-regulated learning cyclical model" are forethought (goal setting and strategy identification), performance monitoring (self-monitoring, self-control, help seeking), and reflection on performance (self-evaluation and self-satisfaction). The article maps these phases onto Levelt-based stages of speech production: conceptualization aligns with forethought, formulation and articulation with performance, and self-monitoring with self-reflection. This mapping justifies teaching planning, monitoring, and evaluation strategies in speaking classes.
requirements: Teachers must explicitly teach and model the strategies for each phase before students apply them
constraints: The framework is applied to speaking classes in a foreign-language university context
target_learning_goals: speaking proficiency
self-regulated learning

title: Zimmerman's three-phase model of self-regulated learning
description: The article adopts Zimmerman's three-phase model of self-regulation as its framework for self-regulated learning. The first phase, forethought, covers "the skilled and strategic processes that precede and set the stage for performance in learning", including goal setting, attribution, self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation. The performance control phase includes attention, affect, monitoring of action, time management, task strategies and help seeking; the self-reflection phase involves evaluating performance outcomes and adjusting skills and strategies. The study measures self-regulated learning against this framework.
requirements: Learners must be metacognitively, motivationally, and behaviorally active participants in their own learning processes
constraints: The article states self-regulation is context specific according to social cognitive theory
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning
goal setting
self-monitoring
self-evaluation
examples: The study's self-regulated learning scale (Purdie, adapted by Ahmad, 2007) measures domains such as planning and goals, monitoring, understanding, and social helping

article_title: Investigating the role of self-assessment in enhancing self-regulated learning amongst medical students in problem-based learning.
citation: Khoiriyah Umatul, Roberts Chris. (2025). Investigating the role of self-assessment in enhancing self-regulated learning amongst medical students in problem-based learning. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07359-5
title: Zimmerman's three-phase self-regulated learning cycle (forethought, performance, self-reflection)
description: The article adopts Zimmerman's SRL framework as its theoretical lens, describing SRL as "a cyclic process encompassing three interconnected phases: forethought, performance, and self-reflection". The forethought phase covers task analysis and self-motivational beliefs including self-efficacy and goal orientation; the performance phase covers self-control and self-observation; the self-reflection phase covers self-evaluation against standards or peers, which the article calls self-assessment. The study maps the observed effects of structured self-assessment onto all three phases in the PBL context.
requirements: The framework is used with a socio-cognitive lens in which social and cognitive aspects of learning interact, supported by triangulated data sources
constraints: The article applies the framework to novice medical students in PBL tutorials
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning skills including motivation, learning strategies, and management of learning resources
examples: The study mapped motivation gains to the forethought phase, self-monitoring to the performance phase, and self-judgement and self-reaction to the self-reflection phase

article_title: Self-regulated learning lens on trainee perceptions of the mini-CEX: a qualitative study.
citation: Kipen Eva, Flynn Eleanor, Woodward-Kron Robyn. (2019). Self-regulated learning lens on trainee perceptions of the mini-CEX: a qualitative study. BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2018-026796
title: Zimmerman's self-regulated learning framework as an interpretive lens for workplace-based assessment
description: The study applies Zimmerman's social cognitive model of self-regulated learning, in which self-regulation is "an interaction of personal, behavioural and environmental triadic processes" and comprises a forethought phase, a performance phase and a self-reflection phase. Self-regulation is cyclical because feedback from prior performance informs adjustments in current or future efforts. The authors use this framework to sensitise their thematic analysis and to re-interpret the existing mini-CEX literature in a holistic, contextualised way.
requirements: Interpretation of assessment experiences requires attention to the covert integration of personal, interpersonal and contextual influences on a trainee's SRL
constraints: The article applies the framework as an interpretive lens on recalled trainee experiences in geriatric medicine training in Melbourne, not as a tested model
target_learners: postgraduate advanced trainees in geriatric medicine
target_learning_goals: self-regulated learning during workplace-based clinical assessment
examples: The three interview themes of goal setting, task translation and perceived outcome were mapped onto the forethought, performance and self-reflection phases respectively
